To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the functional and pharmacologic characteristics of NMDARs on 12 DIC granule neurons are heterogeneous and that NMDA receptor antagonists protect these neurons from glutamate-induced toxicity.
NMDA receptor binding sites on 12 DIC rat cerebellar neurons are a heterogeous population that mediate glutamate toxicity.

NMDA receptor binding sites on 12 DIC cultured cerebellar granular neurons are a heterogeneous population of high- and/or low-affinity sites that are functionally involved in mediating glutamate neurotoxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model of NMDA-mediated neurotoxicity in cerebellar granular cells in culture.
the characterization and regulation of NMDARs on cerebellar neurons in vitro, and their role in mediating glutamate toxicity.
understanding the molecular mechanisms of NMDA-mediated excitatory neurotransmission in the central nervous system, and the role of these receptors in glutamate-mediated neuronal toxicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NMDA receptors expressed by cerebellar granular neurons in culture are heterogeneous and are composed of subunits with different pharmacological and functional properties.
NMDA channels on 12 DIC neurons are a heterogonous population, but the functional role of these receptors in glutamate-induced neurodegeneration is mediated by the high-affinity sites.
the NMDA receptor channel is a heteromeric complex that undergoes developmentally regulated changes in subunit composition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NMDA receptors of cerebellar neurons in culture are developmentally regulated and are involved in the mechanism of glutamate-mediated toxicity.
NMDA channels are composed of different subunit combinations and the different channels are expressed at different times during the development of the granule neurons.
NMDA receptor-mediated toxicity in cerebellar granulocytes is mediated by a high-affinity NMDA receptor population that is pharmacologically distinct from a low-affinity population.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the NMDA receptors expressed by granule neurons at this developmental stage are pharmacologically similar to those expressed by neurons in other regions of the brain, and they mediate the neurotoxic effects of glutamate in vitro.
MK-801 is a very potent neuroprotective drug.
the NMDA receptor channel blocker MK-801 protects cerebellar granules from glutamate induced toxicity, and the NMDA receptors are heterogenous in their binding properties.
